claims.title: Arbitrary-center area converse for Bell visibility-phase renderers: N_w(eps) >= pi/(A_w eps^2)
claims.scope: rank-2 coplanar Bell schedules, renderer states emitting arbitrary laws on settings x outcomes, all q in the unit disk
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
each renderer state emits one fixed law, not necessarily in the family or with setting marginal w
nonclaims: the volumetric covering argument and Brunn's central-section principle are classical; new only as applied to off-family Bell renderers
not a multi-trial or adaptive transcript bound
the area converse is not claimed tight for non-tiling polar bodies; for tiling schedules an optimal packing already gives the same constant

claims.title: Sharp canonical CHSH renderer count with constant pi/32: pi/(32 eps^2) <= N <= pi(1 + 8 eps)^2/(32 eps^2), with an in-family upper bound for eps <= 1/8
claims.scope: canonical equal-weight CHSH schedule, eps > 0 (eps <= 1/8 for the in-family annulus bound), arbitrary-center and in-family covers of the unit disk
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
clipped-center emissions are admissible for the arbitrary-center count
nonclaims: the lower constant pi/32 also follows from ST-T05 packing and the square tiling; the 1/16 -> pi/32 change is over the ST-T13 inscribed-square construction, and is asymptotic (at eps = 3/25 ST-T13 gives the larger finite bound); the new part is the matching upper bound
clipped-center laws are not claimed quantum-realizable
internal predictive bits are not parent-hardware bits

claims.title: Universal pi^3 lower bound on the polar-zonotope area (classical polar-area/perimeter inequality specialized to per(Z) = 2)
claims.scope: every finite coplanar schedule (strict inequality); trivial (A_w = +infinity) in rank 1; equality only for the isotropic generalized schedule under the setting-measurable extension
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
nonclaims: equivalent to Lutwak's planar dual mixed-volume inequality (Pacific J. Math. 58 (1975)); standard argument (Cauchy's perimeter formula and Jensen), not claimed as new
bounds only the area converse; the true renderer constant can exceed 1/pi^2 by a covering-density factor

claims.title: Exact renderer asymptotics for two- and three-direction (tiling) schedules: N_w(eps) eps^2 -> pi/A_w for arbitrary and in-family emissions
claims.scope: rank-2 schedules with exactly 2 or 3 direction classes
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
classical fact that centrally symmetric planar hexagons and parallelograms are lattice tiles (Fedorov), cited
nonclaims: the covering asymptotics for lattice tiles are classical and the lower bound for tiling schedules also follows from ST-T05 packing; the new content is the matching for arbitrary (off-family) emissions via ST-T290 and clipping
no exact constant for arbitrary emissions with 4 or more direction classes (ST-O05)
a one-class schedule has N_w(eps) = O(1/eps), constant 0

claims.title: Regular three-direction schedule uniquely minimizes the polar area among rank-2 schedules with 2 or 3 classes: 2-class minimum 32 (orthogonal equal weights, CHSH), 3-class minimum 18 sqrt3 (regular)
claims.scope: rank-2 schedules with 2 or 3 direction classes; uniqueness is of the law on direction classes, up to rotation
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
nonclaims: the regular hexagon schedule is not the global optimum over all schedules (ST-T295)

the constants depend only on the class law, not on whether a setting realization admits a Bell violation: Alice {0} with Bob {0, -pi/3, -2pi/3} admits none, while the 3x3 uniform trine product schedule realizes the same class law and contains a CHSH test with |S| = 5v/2; no 2x2 product schedule realizes the optimum
the discrete isoperimetric literature was not searched exhaustively; priority for the 3-class inequality is not asserted

claims.title: Covering-density bracket pi/A_w <= liminf N_w eps^2 <= limsup N_w eps^2 <= theta_L(Z°) pi/A_w <= 2/(sqrt27 pi), and non-optimality of tiling schedules (the regular 4-direction schedule beats the hexagon)
claims.scope: all rank-2 finite schedules and, under setting-measurable emissions, the isotropic generalized schedule
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
L. Fejes Toth's centrally symmetric lattice covering bound 2pi/sqrt27 (via Sas 1939), cited, not reproved
the asymptotic covering theorem for translates (Rogers 1964), cited
nonclaims: the in-family limit theta_T(Z°) pi/A_w is classical (asymptotic covering theorem); the identification theta_T = theta_L = |K|/|h(K)| for centrally symmetric discs is cited from the literature and not verified here
the bracket is not an exact value for arbitrary emissions
the global memory-forcing optimum schedule is not identified

claims.title: Centre Fisher isotropy ties CHSH and every regular schedule (I(0) = I/2) while their memory constants differ
claims.scope: Fisher information at q = 0 for one randomized-setting trial; regular m-direction schedules, m >= 2
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
nonclaims: an elementary design-optimality computation (sum of cos(2 theta_k) and sin(2 theta_k) vanish), not claimed as new; exact checks cover m <= 4
no claim about Fisher rankings away from the centre

claims.title: Bounded exact Bell-disk zonoid audit
claims.scope: exact Q(sqrt2), Q(sqrt3) and rational checks: polar areas, CHSH grid counts for eps = 1/40..1/400, clipped-centre covers, served-set areas, 62468-case hexagon grid, polynomial lemma samples, trine product schedule
assumptions: all certifying comparisons use exact arithmetic with rational pi and sqrt enclosures
nonclaims: bounded checks are not the asymptotic theorems
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation

claims.title: Exact renderer constant for arbitrary (off-family) emissions on non-tiling Bell schedules
claims.scope: schedules with 4 or more direction classes, including the isotropic schedule: existence of lim N_w eps^2 and its value; known: liminf >= pi/A_w and limsup <= theta_L(Z°) pi/A_w
assumptions: P(a,b|x,y,v,phi) = 1/4[1 - ab v cos(alpha_x - beta_y - phi)] with q = (v cos phi, v sin phi) in the closed unit disk (ST-T11)
settings are drawn externally from a fixed finite schedule w with positive weights; accuracy is one-trial total variation
nonclaims: the in-family constant is classical (ST-T295); only the arbitrary-emission constant is open
no exact constant is currently claimed

claims.title: Discrete dual-isoperimetric inequality per(P)^2 area(P°) >= 2 n^3 tan^2(pi/n) sin(2pi/n) for convex n-gons containing the origin
claims.scope: convex n-gons P containing the origin; the centrally symmetric n = 4, 6 cases are ST-T294
assumptions: float experiments during review found no violation for n = 3..6
nonclaims: not proved; the literature was not searched thoroughly, so the statement may be known
